## 2. Where the fix belongs, and the precedent search

Where it belongs. The tower is a library shape: walk reads Library/FortressLibrary.fsi and .fss and ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fsi and .fss, and converts by coercion at a parameter, an overloaded call and a typed binding already (FACTS.md, "Under walk, the interpreter converts by coercion at its three kinds of type check"), so no Java change was needed and none was made; the glue classes Int.java, Long.java, NN32.java and UnsignedLong.java are untouched. The compiled path runs its own prelude (Library/CompilerLibrary.*, CompilerAlgebra.*, CompilerSystem.*, ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.*), which this rung does not touch; its ladder is measured in section 15.

What the team already did here, by citation, and what I followed:
- The flat shape itself: the compiler prelude declares its integer types as siblings with a coerce on each wider type (ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fsi:103-108, ZZ from IntLiteral, ZZ32, ZZ64, NN32 and NN64; :147-149, ZZ64 from IntLiteral and ZZ32; :332-334, NN64 from IntLiteral and NN32). Followed for the header shape (a sibling extending Number with excludes) and for putting each coercion on the wider type, which the specification requires (Specification/basic/conversions-coercions.tex:176-187). The interpreter library had no coerce declaration before this rung (git show e5414f5bf:Library/FortressLibrary.fss has none), so these are its first.
- The identity from the static argument: the () -> T witness typecase the library already uses in array1 (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2282-2286 at e5414f5bf, now :2342-2346), as answer 7 prescribes, in the form of the judgement's library copy (explorations/reviews/sum-replacement-judgement/variants/sumlib.py:22-37: narrowest leaf first, else => 0 and else => 1), with each branch's value through the library's own cast[\T\] (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:34-38 at e5414f5bf), as explorations/reviews/sum-replacement-verdict.md proposes. Followed; the leaves listed are all eight number leaves, each before any supertype (section 5.3).
- The specification's own shape for a clause-form sum: the wrapper SUM[\N\] with SumReduction[\N\] (Specification/advanced/parallelism-locality/defining-generators.tex:147-157). Followed: SumReduction and ProdReduction are generic in their element type.
- The price of the flattening measured on a library copy: 14 declaration headers and 15 inherited methods the leaves must state (explorations/reviews/mie-probes/price-keep-the-rule.md sections 1, 2 and 6; explorations/reviews/mie-probes/keep/flat-tower-sketch.fsi, an excerpt). Followed for which methods move from Number to the leaves; deviated where section 6 says.
- Retyping a native's parameter from Number to its own type: RR32's natives take b:Number (git show e5414f5bf:ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:257-339); Float's comparison natives already take Float and RR64 (ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:54-130). Followed Float's shape for RR32 (section 5.7).
- The comparison runner and its normalisation: rung O's count-run.sh and rung D's compare-normalised.py (explorations/compile-ladder/rung-walk-overflow/REPORT.md section 2; explorations/compile-ladder/rung-wrap-operators/compare-normalised.py), copied into this directory unchanged but for paths; the classification of the 17 unstable tests follows rung O's (explorations/compile-ladder/rung-walk-overflow/REPORT.md:40). The ladder subset driver is rung D's run-subset.sh with a source-directory variable (explorations/compile-ladder/rung-flat-tower/run-subset.sh).
- A precedent that repaired a defect is evidence of the same defect elsewhere: row 146's shape (a ZZ64 declared, a ZZ32 held) is the shape of row 428 (Ratio's num: ZZ holding a Long); both close by the same means, the typed binding converting by coercion once ZZ64 and ZZ are not supertypes of ZZ32 (section 5.5). I counted the other sites of the shape "declared a wider integer type, bound from a numeral" in the library: every one is now converted by the typed binding's coercion, which walk applies at each (FACTS.md, three kinds of type check); the ones that needed an explicit conversion instead are listed in section 5.6.

Names added, grepped for competing declarations in ProjectFortress/tests/, every ProjectFortress/*_tests/ directory, ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/ and Library/: additiveIdentity, multiplicativeIdentity, exactValue, FlatTowerRungF. None found outside the library's own declaration.

## 3. The specification's derivation

- The tower. Instantiation exclusion (Specification/basic/types-vals-vars.tex:218-237) forbids a type below two instantiations of one generic, so ZZ32 cannot be both an Integral[\ZZ32\] and, through ZZ64, an Integral[\ZZ64\]; route A (POSITIONS.md:92) makes the leaves siblings. The number chapters still describe the nested tower (Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex, basic-integers.tex); they are rung T's.
- The coercions. Declared by the wider type (Specification/basic/conversions-coercions.tex:176-187), not inherited (:224-227), not chained (:127-132), so each pair of the table is declared on its own; a coercion applies only where the parameter's declared type is exactly the coerced-to type (:78-83), which settles two of the Q1 lines (section 9: longPrim's DIVIDES, whose self is an Integral[\ZZ64\], not a ZZ64). The table is the record's and nothing else: ZZ64 from ZZ32 and NN32; NN64 from NN32; ZZ from ZZ32, ZZ64, NN32 and NN64; QQ from the five integer types; RR64 from ZZ32. NN32 into RR64 stays explicit, and no site needed it.
- The algebra. ZZ is "a commutative ring and is totally ordered" (Specification/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:79), so Integral[\I\] extends MultiplicativeRing[\I\] as well as StandardTotalOrder[\I\]; that is what admits the integer types to PROD's bound (decision D2).
- Exact rationals. "Rational computations do not overflow" (Specification/basic/operators/opr-overview.tex:156, :197); numerator and denominator are declared ZZ (Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, QQ), so their products are unbounded.
- Equality across number types. "The comparison operators <, <=, =, >= and > allow any rational value to be compared numerically to any other rational value" (Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex:372-373); the integers are rationals in that chapter. This is the ground for decision D1.
- The reductions. A reduction expression takes optional static arguments (Specification/basic/expressions/reductions.tex:15-26), and the specification's desugaring of a clause-form sum is SUM[\N\] over SumReduction[\N\] (Specification/advanced/parallelism-locality/defining-generators.tex:147-157). Nothing in Specification/basic/ says how N is found when no argument fixes it; answer 7 has a clause form write it, and rung T writes the note (reductions.tex:23-25).
- Silent: whether a list literal of numerals has an element type an F-bounded big operator accepts. A numeral has type NaturalNumeral[\n,10,v\] and Literal[\v\], with the relation to the integer types left open in a note (Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:83-86), and a list expression's element type is the union of its elements' types (Specification/basic/expressions/aggregate.tex:105); so the specification does not say whether SUM <|1, 2, 3|> finds T = ZZ32. That is why section 12.3's refusal has home 3.
EOF

- The tower. Instantiation exclusion (Specification/basic/types-vals-vars.tex:218-237) forbids a type below two instantiations of one generic, so ZZ32 cannot be both an Integral[\ZZ32\] and, through ZZ64, an Integral[\ZZ64\]; route A (POSITIONS.md:92) makes the leaves siblings. The number chapters still describe the nested tower (Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex, basic-integers.tex); they are rung T's.
- The coercions. Declared by the wider type (Specification/basic/conversions-coercions.tex:176-187), not inherited (:224-227), not chained (:127-132), so each pair of the table is declared on its own; a coercion applies only where the parameter's declared type is exactly the coerced-to type (:78-83), which settles two of the Q1 lines (section 9: longPrim's DIVIDES, whose self is an Integral[\ZZ64\], not a ZZ64). The table is the record's and nothing else: ZZ64 from ZZ32 and NN32; NN64 from NN32; ZZ from ZZ32, ZZ64, NN32 and NN64; QQ from the five integer types; RR64 from ZZ32. A reduction expression takes optional static arguments (Specification/basic/expressions/reductions.tex:15-26), and the specification's desugaring of a clause-form sum is SUM[\N\] over SumReduction[\N\] (Specification/advanced/parallelism-locality/defining-generators.tex:147-157). Alternative: Number without =, as route A's "Number without its catch-all operators" reads literally. Not taken because the library's own opr =(a:Any, b:Any) = a SEQV b would then answer every mixed comparison, so 3 = 3.0 and widen(3) = big(3) would be false with no error, and team tests that compare numbers of different run-time types (CovariantTest's List[\Number\] against List[\ZZ32\], assert(x, y) over mixed values) would change silently; and the specification says rationals compare numerically (Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex:372-373). This is a decision for Pavol's eye: it is one declaration more on Number than "without its catch-alls".
- D2. Integral[\I\] extends MultiplicativeRing[\I\] beside StandardTotalOrder[\I\] (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:644), so the integers meet PROD's bound and have a one. Alternative: the flat sketch's AdditiveGroup only, which would leave PROD[\ZZ32\] outside its bound. Ground: "ZZ is a commutative ring" (Specification/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:79). The integration review warned that MultiplicativeRing's ^ answers T while the integers' ^ answers RR64 (explorations/reviews/numeric-hierarchy-integration-review.md section 2); walk does not check that, and the checker's body-level errors (section 13) show no new one from it; it is noted, not solved.
- D3. Integer / always answers a Ratio, and a Ratio whose denominator is 1 prints as its numerator (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:628-629). On the base, ZZ's / answered a ZZ when the quotient was whole (git show e5414f5bf:Library/FortressLibrary.fss:891-897), which a QQ-typed / can no longer do, a ZZ not being a QQ. Alternative: print n/1. Not taken because every whole quotient the tests print would change ("3" to "3/1"); with this spelling none did.
- D4. Integral[\I\] keeps AnyIntegral among its supertypes. Alternative: drop it, which the checker's comprises rule would prefer ("AnyIntegral has a comprises clause but its immediate subtype Integral is not eligible to extend it", reported before and after). Not taken because without it walk's overload check refuses C4's generic array operators beside Integral's generic ones (the arrays exclude Number, and so AnyIntegral, only through that link), and the microGPT check failed; with it both checks pass 40 of 40.
- D5. Number keeps a comprises clause, { RR64, QQ, AnyIntegral }. Alternative: none, as route A does not ask for one. Not taken because walk's overload check needs the exclusions it gives to accept the scalar-extension MAX beside StandardTotalOrder's generic MAX ("excluding types"), as today's comprises { RR64 } gave them.
- D6. asFloat(self): RR64 is published in Number's api; it was a component-only method. Alternative: a new conversion function. Not taken: the library's bodies already use asFloat, and Library/String.fss and the respelled tests need it visible.
- D7. RR32's natives take RR64 where they took Number, and RR32's and Float's MIN, MAX and MINMAX answer RR64 (section 5.7). Alternative: keep Number parameters, which walk's overload check refuses beside RR64's own operators once Number declares none.
- D8. The identity witness has eight branches, the number leaves narrowest first with RR32 before RR64, and keeps the judgement's else => 0 and else => 1 (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3117, :3130). Alternative: else => cast[\T\](0), which the checker would type as T, or a throw. Not taken, to follow the judgement's measured copy (explorations/reviews/sum-replacement-judgement/variants/sumlib.py:27, :35); the checker reports one error on each ("Function body has type OR(T,IntLiteral), but declared return type is T", section 13). The branch values go through cast[\T\], as the verdict proposes.
- D9. The fusion pairs SumProdReductionPair, MaxSumReductionPair and MinSumReductionPair and SumReduction's two distribute overloads are restated generic, not dropped; the judgement allowed either ("restated in T or dropped for the rung", explorations/reviews/sum-replacement-judgement.md, section 4 A). Kept because Library/Generator2.fss:73 and :168 call r.distribute(q), and Generator2Test's maximum prefix sum takes the fused path with them. Cost, measured: the checker reports the restated types ill-formed, 6 reports at 4 sites (MaxReduction[\T\] and MinReduction[\T\] in SumReduction's distribute, MaxSumReductionPair[\T\] and MinSumReductionPair[\T\] in their bodies), because T extends AdditiveGroup[\T\] does not give StandardMax[\T\]. The specification's remedy is a where clause on the method (Specification/basic/trait-parameters.tex:285-310), which "are not supported yet" (Specification/basic/functions.tex:15-19); provisional row 433.
- D10. genZZ.perturb keeps the base's 64-bit shift, big(widen(obj) LSHIFT 32) (Library/QuickCheck.fss:322). Alternative: RSHIFT 32, which is what peeling 32 bits at a time evidently means. Not taken because it changes the generated values of every QuickCheck test that reaches it; provisional row 431 records the defect.
- D11. additiveIdentity, multiplicativeIdentity and exactValue are component-private (not in the api). Alternative: publish them; nothing outside the library needs them.
- D12. strToFloat converts the quotient with asFloat and keeps the approved SUM[\ZZ32\] (its elements are Ints: walk's ZZ32 ^ answers an Int, probes/strtofloat-flat-after.txt "10^k : Int"). Alternative: SUM[\RR64\] over converted terms, which departs from the approved list.
- D13. The team-test respellings (section 9): typed comprehensions (<|[\ZZ32\] ...|>) where a list's element type walk takes from run-time classes fails a new F-bound; asFloat where a value relied on ZZ64, ZZ, QQ or Number reaching RR64; widen where a ZZ32 met a generic Integral method or a generic function's ZZ64 parameter; List[\Number\] where a list mixes integers and floats. Alternative for each: the smallest other spelling that keeps the value, e.g. a float literal (fib13, vectorOps, asifTest took that form where it keeps the value).
EOF
echo ok

After the flattening Number supplies none of these capabilities: it declares asFloat and = only. Each leaf supplies them itself: the five integer types through Integral[\I\] (MultiplicativeRing[\I\], so AdditiveGroup[\I\], and StandardTotalOrder[\I\], so StandardMinMax[\I\]), QQ and RR64 through their own AdditiveGroup, MultiplicativeRing and StandardMinMax at their own type. So each body is justified per leaf at run time, and not by its bound, which is the integration review's point; the body-level check (section 13) shows the checker agrees.

| Operation (Library/FortressLibrary.fss) | The body needs | Base, 7 leaves | Flat, 7 leaves |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vector + and - (:2294-2297) | T + T : T, T - T : T | all run | all run |
| Vector unary - (:2298) | -T : T | all | all |
| Vector.scale (:2299), pmul (:2300-2301), scalar DOT and juxtaposition (:2369-2380) | T T : T | all | all |
| Vector.dot (:2302-2303), DOT and juxtaposition of two vectors (:2363-2368), squaredNorm (:2381) | an additive identity, T + T, T T (SUM[\T\], whose own bound is AdditiveGroup[\T\]) | all | all |
| the norm (:2383) | the above, then a conversion into RR64 and SQRT | all (Number's SQRT) | all, with asFloat (section 5.8); ZZ64, NN32, NN64, ZZ and QQ were refused before that edit |
| Matrix + and -, unary - (:2602-2606) | T + T, T - T, -T | all | all |
| Matrix.scale (:2607) | T T : T | all | all |
| Matrix.mul and the matrix products (:2608-2650, :2723-2734) | T T and T + T; no identity (mm puts the first product, mma adds to it) | all | all |
| Matrix.rmul and lmul (:2651-2660) | an additive identity, T + T, T T (SUM[\T\]) | all | all |
| Matrix.t() (:2661) | nothing | all | all |
| matrix(v) (:2717-2718) | a zero of T, written as the numeral 0 | ZZ32, ZZ64, ZZ, QQ, RR64; refused for NN32 and NN64 | the same: 0 reaches T by T's coercion from ZZ32, which NN32 and NN64 do not declare; the site shares its declaration with fill and goes to phase 3 with tabulate (the record, section 1) |
| scalar-extension +, - (:4574-4580) | T + T, T - T | all | all |
| scalar-extension MIN, MAX (:4581-4584) | StandardMin[\T\], StandardMax[\T\] | all | all |

The approved model lines are not of this shape (C4's sums are over typed arrays and ranges). The specification does not settle the element type of a list of numerals (section 3), so this is provisional row 432, home 3.

# Rung F (`rung-flat-tower`): record lines for the gather

Written by the rung worker for the coordinator's fold. `<F>` stands for the landed commit. Row numbers from 431 are provisional; the gather assigns the final numbers in manifest order (F, T, R). The rung met none of the stops the batch record's intro
 reserves for Pavol; three things in the report are for his eye (REPORT.md section 1): bare big operators over numeral lists (row 432), the compile ladder's two changes from test lines (section 15), and decision D1, Number's numeric `=`.

## FACTS.md

Under "Landed semantics", a new entry after "The specification's wrapping operators ∔, ∸ and ⨰ ...":

- **The one library's number tower is flat** (2026-09-27, climb batch 6 rung F, `<F>`; `compile-ladder/rung-flat-tower/`; rows 146, 423, 428). `ZZ32`, `ZZ64`, `NN32`, `NN64`, `ZZ`, `QQ` and `RR64` are siblings under `Number` (`Number comprises { RR64
, QQ, AnyIntegral }`, `AnyIntegral comprises { ZZ, ZZ64, ZZ32, NN64, NN32 }`), each carrying its own algebra: `RR64` and `QQ` extend `StandardPartialOrder`, `StandardMinMax`, `AdditiveGroup` and `MultiplicativeRing` at their own type, and `Integral[\
I\]` extends `StandardTotalOrder[\I\]`, `MultiplicativeRing[\I\]` and `AnyIntegral` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:276-606`; `NN32` in `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fsi`). Each wider type declares `coerce` from each narrower one, exa
ctly the record's table: `ZZ64` from `ZZ32` and `NN32`; `NN64` from `NN32`; `ZZ` from the four fixed widths; `QQ` from all five integer types; `RR64` from `ZZ32` (and so from every numeral that fits it) and from nothing else. `Number` declares only `
asFloat(self): RR64` (now in the api) and one numeric `opr =`: two exact numbers compare as rationals, a float with any number through `asFloat` (`Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex:372-373`). `ZZ64`, `NN32`, `NN64`, `ZZ` and `QQ` reach `RR64` only 
by an explicit `asFloat`; integer `/` always answers a `Ratio`, which prints without `/1`. `SUM` and `PROD` are generic reductions over `AdditiveGroup[\T\]` and `MultiplicativeRing[\T\]` whose identity comes from the static argument through a `() -> 
T` witness `typecase` over the eight number leaves, narrowest first; a clause form whose element type no argument fixes writes it (`SUM[\ZZ32\][j <- 0#i] ...`), and an unwritten empty one now raises `CastError` (row 424). `BIG MAXN`, `BIG MINN` and `
BIG MINMAXN` are gone. `QQ`'s arithmetic is exact, its parts always `BigNum`s (row 428); a `ZZ64` bound to a numeral holds 64 bits (row 146). Under `walk`, a bare big operator over a list literal of numerals is refused (row 432), and a `ZZ32` scalar 
meets an `RR64` array or matrix in a generic operator only when written as a float (row 388). Gated by `ProjectFortress/tests/FlatTowerRungF.fss`. Of 407 interpreter tests, 383 print the same, 4 the same once normalised, 17 vary on their own; 3 chang
ed with stated causes (Region, a coercion applied; simpleBig, a respelled line; XXXArrayLiteralArgRungC, its message's overload list); no exit code changed; 89 team-test lines respelled (24 approved, 65 under Q1 = (a)). The two microGPT checks pass 4
0 of 40 with the same printed values. The checker count is 62, from 125.

Under "The checker and the one library", appended to the entry "The true distance to the switch-over": *On the landed flat library (climb batch 6 rung F, `<F>`), the count stage is 62 (the 18 errors above the flattened copy's 44 are the hierarchy err
ors at `TotalComparison` and at `AnyMaybe`, `Maybe`, `Just` and `Nothing`), and the distance driver's component total for `FortressLibrary` under walk's setting is 1,948, from 3,186 on the base, printed totals not deduplicated (`compile-ladder/rung-f
lat-tower/probes/distance/stage-counts.txt`).*

Under "The library's arrays and algebra", appended to "Route A's generic container obligations still need body-level checks": *Measured by climb batch 6 rung F (`<F>`; `compile-ladder/rung-flat-tower/REPORT.md` sections 12 and 13): every operation of
 `Vector`, `Matrix` and the scalar-extension block runs under `walk` for all seven leaves (the norm with an explicit `asFloat`), except `matrix(v)` for `NN32` and `NN64` as before, because its numeral `0` reaches `T` by coercion; the checker now refu
ses the generic bodies' arithmetic at `(T, T)` ("Could not check call to operator juxtaposition"), where before it typed it as `RR64` against a declared `T`: the obligation is unchanged, its message is not.* And to "The shipped `RR64` does not satisf
y the specification's algebraic bound": *Superseded by climb batch 6 rung F (`<F>`): `RR64` extends `AdditiveGroup[\RR64\]` and `MultiplicativeRing[\RR64\]`.*

Under "The harness and the gate", a new entry:

- **The compile ladder loses one file to an approved test line, until the switch-over** (2026-09-27, climb batch 6 rung F, `<F>`; `compile-ladder/rung-flat-tower/REPORT.md` section 15). `ProjectFortress/tests/CoercionRedispatchRungC.fss` compiled and
 ran on the compiled path before; with answer 7's `SUM[\ZZ32\]` at its line 43 the compiler refuses it, "Wrong number or kind of static arguments for function: BIG +", because the compiler prelude's `SUM` takes no static argument (`Library/CompilerLi
brary.fsi:180-181`), the reason `BigSumRung8` waits; and `expTest.fss`'s first error moves from typecheck to disambiguate on `asFloat`, which the prelude does not declare. `walk`'s gated run needs both spellings, so the files cannot satisfy both path
s until one library serves both.

## Ledger

- **Row 423**, appended to its notes, and closed: "Closed `<F>` (climb batch 6, rung F): the block is dropped, `BIG MAXN`, `BIG MINN`, `BIG MINMAXN`, `MaxReductionN`, `MinReductionN`, `MinMaxReductionN`, `MaxNSumReductionPair`, `MinNSumReductionPair`
, the `distribute` overloads and the `DistributesOver` clauses that named them, in the api and the component, so both slips go with it. Their identity was the rational `-1/0` or `1/0`, a value no integer or float fold can hold, and a maximum's identi
ty is not carried by a coercion (`reviews/max-min-identities-judgement.md` sections 1 and 4; POSITIONS.md:168). No name of them is left in `Library/`, the tests or the demos; the judgement's own probe `reviews/max-min-identities-judgement/MaxMinWalk.
fss` records what they did and no longer runs."
- **Row 428**, appended, and closed: "Fixed `<F>` (climb batch 6, rung F): on the flat tower every value reaching a `Ratio`'s `num: ZZ` or `den: ZZ` is converted to a `BigNum` by `ZZ`'s coercions, so `numerator` and `denominator` answer `BigNum`s and
 the cross-products of `<`, `+`, `DOT` and `/` cannot wrap; `QQ`'s operator text is unchanged. `(widen(1) LSHIFT 62) < 1/4` and `(widen(1) LSHIFT 61)/3 < 5/7` are `false`, and `+`, `DOT` and `/` beyond 32 bits are exact: home 1, `ProjectFortress/test
s/FlatTowerRungF.fss:122-129`. For rung O: `ReflectiveQuickCheckTest` passes on the flat library in every pass."
- **Row 146**, appended, and closed: "Fixed `<F>` (climb batch 6, rung F): `x: ZZ64 = 2147483647` holds a `Long` by `ZZ64`'s coercion from `ZZ32` at the typed binding, and `x + 1` is `2147483648`: home 1, `ProjectFortress/tests/FlatTowerRungF.fss:41-
42`."
- **Row 135**, appended: "Climb batch 6, rung F (`<F>`): the library's eleven clause-form sums write their static argument (`SUM[\T\]` in `Vector.dot`, `Matrix.rmul`, `Matrix.lmul` and `Sparse.fss:96`; `SUM[\ZZ32\]` in `strToInt`, `strToFloat`, `Chun
kedSparseArray.fss:161`, `:163`, `PrefixMap.fss:380`, `PrefixSet.fss:374`, `SkipList.fss:208`), as the team's `BIG UNION[\String,ZZ32\]` does, and so do the 24 approved team-test lines and the Q1 lines that meet the same need (`compile-ladder/rung-fl
at-tower/probes/test-lines.txt`; REPORT.md section 9)."
- **Row 424**, appended: "Climb batch 6, rung F (`<F>`): with answer 7's `SUM` landed, an unwritten clause form fails under `walk` at its first element as this row says, and an unwritten *empty* one raises `CastError`, since `T` is `Bottom`, the witn
ess takes its first branch, and `cast[\Bottom\](0)` fails (`compile-ladder/rung-flat-tower/probes/unwritten-sum-flat.txt`). Every clause form in the library, the tests and the models writes its argument."
- **Row 426**, appended: "Climb batch 6, rung F (`<F>`): the identity functions pass each branch value through `cast[\T\]`, so the compiled half of the verdict's three outcomes (`reviews/sum-replacement-verdict.md`) waits on this row, or on a checker
 refinement of the witness branch, before the switch-over; `walk`'s half is gated in `ProjectFortress/tests/FlatTowerRungF.fss`, group 3."
- **Row 388**, appended: "Climb batch 6, rung F (`<F>`), the consequence measured (`compile-ladder/rung-flat-tower/probes/row388-base.txt`, `row388-flat.txt`): with an `RR64` matrix `m`, an `RR64` array `a` and a `ZZ32` `i`, `m.scale(i)` runs (a meth
od's declared parameter converts), and `m i`, `i m`, `m DOT i`, `a + i`, `i + a`, `a - i`, `i - a`, `a MIN i` and `i MAX a`, which ran on the nested tower, are refused on the flat one; none is in C4 or the APL program; `vectorOps.fss:27` and `BitTwid
dle.fss:45`, `:47` were respelled for it."
- **Row 330**, appended: "Climb batch 6, rung F (`<F>`): after the flattening, `ZZ`, `ZZ64`, `NN32`, `NN64` and `QQ` reach `RR64` only by an explicit `asFloat`; only `ZZ32` and numerals coerce. An integer result that goes back into float arithmetic n
ow does so by `asFloat`, not by promotion."
- **Row 20**, appended: "Climb batch 6, rung F (`<F>`): on the flat tower this row's run-time element type fails the algebraic F-bounds of `SUM`, `PROD` and `BIG MAX`: a bare big operator over a list literal of numerals is refused (row 432)."
- **Row 295**, appended: "Climb batch 6, rung F (`<F>`): two of this row's findings change on the flat tower. `RR64` now meets `T extends AdditiveGroup[\T\]` (it extends `AdditiveGroup[\RR64\]`); and the scalar-extension block no longer takes an inte
ger into an `RR64` array's slot (`a + i` with `i: ZZ32` is refused, row 388), where a float literal does."

brary bug | none: the specification does not describe `QuickCheck` (grep for QuickCheck under `Specification/basic/` and `Specification/basic-lib/` finds nothing), so home 3 | `compile-ladder/rung-flat-tower/probes/perturb-base-line.txt` (the flat li

# Rung F: the flat tower

problem: the new test's five groups each fail on the nested tower, groups 1 to 4 with a failed assertion and group 5 with a refused call (explorations/compile-ladder/rung-flat-tower/probes/failure-preedit.txt:8-13), and the checker refuses the tower's hierarchy (explorations/compile-ladder/rung-flat-tower/probes/checker-count/table-before.txt:4-5, :14)
spec: instantiation exclusion (Specification/basic/types-vals-vars.tex:218-237); a coercion is declared on the wider type, is not inherited and does not chain (Specification/basic/conversions-coercions.tex:176-187, :224-227, :127-132), and applies at a parameter of exactly the coerced-to type (:78-83); rational computations do not overflow (Specification/basic/operators/opr-overview.tex:156, :197); rationals compare numerically (Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex:372-373); ZZ is a commutative ring (Specification/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:79); a reduction's optional static arguments (Specification/basic/expressions/reductions.tex:15-26)
precedent: the compiler prelude's flat tower and its coerce declarations (ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fsi:103-108, :147-149, :332-334); the () -> T witness typecase of array1 (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2342-2346, :2282-2286 at e5414f5bf); the judgement's option A library copy (explorations/reviews/sum-replacement-judgement/variants/sumlib.py:22-37)
deviation: Number keeps a numeric = across its leaves (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:355-377) where route A removes its catch-alls; Integral extends MultiplicativeRing[\I\] (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:644) where the sketch gives AdditiveGroup (explorations/reviews/mie-probes/keep/flat-tower-sketch.fsi); integer / always answers a Ratio, which prints without /1 (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:628-629); the Max/Min-Sum fusion pairs restated in T are ill-formed to the checker, where clauses being unsupported (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3138-3158; Specification/basic/functions.tex:15-19); the identity witness keeps the judgement's else => 0 (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3117, :3130)
historical: Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, Library/FortressLibrary.fss, Library/ChunkedSparseArray.fss, Library/Format.fss, Library/PrefixMap.fss, Library/PrefixSet.fss, Library/QuickCheck.fss, Library/Random.fss, Library/ReflectiveQuickCheck.fss, Library/SkipList.fss, Library/Sparse.fss, Library/String.fss, Library/Timing.fss, ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fsi, ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss, and in ProjectFortress/tests/ ArrayListQuick.fss, BitTwiddle.fss, CovCollTest.fss, CovariantTest.fss, Generator2Test.fss, ListNullPointer.fss, PureListQuick.fss, ReflectTest.fss, ReflectiveQuickCheckTest.fss, TransactionalArrayShakedown.fss, WordCountSmall.fss, asifTest.fss, expTest.fss, fib13.fss, generatorTest.fss, longPrim.fss, sequivTest.fss, setSum.fss, simpleBig.fss, simpleSum.fss, vectorOps.fss (flagged at commit time, explorations/protocol.md:126-127)

## 0. How this report reaches the tree

The subagent harness refused the worker's write of this file ("Subagents should return findings as text, not write report files"), as it refused every rung worker's in batch 5. Its text is carried word for word in the structured result's reportText, for the gather to write. Everything it cites under explorations/compile-ladder/rung-flat-tower/ is committed on wip/rung-flat-tower.

The rung was one worker's run across context compactions, not a relaunch; nothing was inherited from another attempt. The last compaction came after the three passes, the microGPT checks, the checker count and the first body-level runs; after it I re-read the branch, re-ran the checker count (same table), and then made three more library edits, the third in two steps, all in Library/FortressLibrary.fss bodies (section 5.8), so everything that reads the library was run again on the landed library, c02b558c1: the edit pass (a third edit pass, against the same two base passes), the two microGPT checks, the body-level check and the new test at both thread counts; and on aa6ae506a, which differs from c02b558c1 only in exactValue's clause form, the four-thread differential, row 388's probe and the capability probe.

## 1. Result

The one library's number tower is flat. ZZ32, ZZ64, NN32, NN64, ZZ, QQ and RR64 are siblings under Number, each with its own algebra; each wider type declares the coercions of the record's table and no other; Number declares only asFloat and a numeric =; SUM and PROD are answer 7's typed reductions with the () -> T witness; BIG MAXN, BIG MINN and BIG MINMAXN are gone with their objects, fusion pairs and distribute overloads, in the api as in the component; QQ's arithmetic is exact (row 428); a ZZ64 bound to a numeral holds 64 bits (row 146). The new test ProjectFortress/tests/FlatTowerRungF.fss fails on the base in all five groups and passes at FORTRESS_THREADS=1 and =4.

Of the 407 other interpreter tests, 383 print the same in all three passes, 4 are equal once normalised, 17 vary between the two base runs on their own (timings, random data, thread interleaving, as rung O found the same 17) and 3 changed, each for a stated cause: Region (a coercion now applied), simpleBig (a respelled line) and XXXArrayLiteralArgRungC (its rc 1 error's overload list). No exit code changed. 89 lines of 25 team tests are respelled: 24 approved by answer 7, 65 under Q1 = (a); none deleted an assertion. The two microGPT checks pass 40 of 40 before and after with the same printed values. The checker count falls from 125 to 62; its crash line stays "none". The body-level check's component total falls from 3,186 to 1,948.

Three things for Pavol's eye, none of them a stop the intro reserves. First, a bare big operator over a list literal of numerals is refused under walk on the flat tower (SUM <|1, 2, 3|>, PROD <|1, 2, 3|>, SUM <|1.5, 2.5|>, SUM <| n^2 | n <- 1#3 |>), where the base ran the three sums and the product; the list's element type is walk's run-time class (row 20), Int, which is not an AdditiveGroup[\Int\]; written with [\ZZ32\] or [\RR64\] each runs (section 12.1, provisional row 432). Second, on the compiled path, which runs its own prelude, the approved line CoercionRedispatchRungC.fss:43 turns that file from compiling and running into "Wrong number or kind of static arguments for function: BIG +", for the reason BigSumRung8 waits: the prelude's SUM has no static parameter (Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi:180-181); and expTest's first error moves from typecheck to disambiguate on asFloat, which the prelude lacks (section 15). Third, Number keeps a numeric = across its leaves, a decision (section 6, D1).

## 2. Where the fix belongs, and the precedent search

Where it belongs. The tower is a library shape: walk reads Library/FortressLibrary.fsi and .fss and ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fsi and .fss, and converts by coercion at a parameter, an overloaded call and a typed binding already (FACTS.md, "Under walk, the interpreter converts by coercion at its three kinds of type check"), so no Java change was needed and none was made; the glue classes Int.java, Long.java, NN32.java and UnsignedLong.java are untouched. The compiled path runs its own prelude (Library/CompilerLibrary.*, CompilerAlgebra.*, CompilerSystem.*, ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.*), which this rung does not touch; its ladder is measured in section 15.

What the team already did here, by citation, and what I followed:
- The flat shape itself: the compiler prelude declares its integer types as siblings with a coerce on each wider type (ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fsi:103-108, ZZ from IntLiteral, ZZ32, ZZ64, NN32 and NN64; :147-149, ZZ64 from IntLiteral and ZZ32; :332-334, NN64 from IntLiteral and NN32). Followed for the header shape (a sibling extending Number with excludes) and for putting each coercion on the wider type, which the specification requires (Specification/basic/conversions-coercions.tex:176-187). The interpreter library had no coerce declaration before this rung (git show e5414f5bf:Library/FortressLibrary.fss has none), so these are its first.
- The identity from the static argument: the () -> T witness typecase the library already uses in array1 (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2282-2286 at e5414f5bf, now :2342-2346), as answer 7 prescribes, in the form of the judgement's library copy (explorations/reviews/sum-replacement-judgement/variants/sumlib.py:22-37: narrowest leaf first, else => 0 and else => 1), with each branch's value through the library's own cast[\T\] (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:33-37), as explorations/reviews/sum-replacement-verdict.md proposes. Followed; the leaves listed are all eight number leaves, each before any supertype (section 5.3).
- The specification's own shape for a clause-form sum: the wrapper SUM[\N\] with SumReduction[\N\] (Specification/advanced/parallelism-locality/defining-generators.tex:147-157). Followed: SumReduction and ProdReduction are generic in their element type.
- The price of the flattening measured on a library copy: 14 declaration headers and 15 inherited methods the leaves must state (explorations/reviews/mie-probes/price-keep-the-rule.md sections 1, 2 and 6; explorations/reviews/mie-probes/keep/flat-tower-sketch.fsi, an excerpt). Followed for which methods move from Number to the leaves; deviated where section 6 says.
- Retyping a native's parameter from Number to its own type: RR32's natives took b:Number (git show e5414f5bf:ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:243-321), where Float's take b:Float (ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:81-154). Followed Float's shape for RR32, at RR64 (section 5.7).
- The comparison runner and its normalisation: rung O's count-run.sh and rung D's compare-normalised.py (explorations/compile-ladder/rung-walk-overflow/REPORT.md section 2; explorations/compile-ladder/rung-wrap-operators/compare-normalised.py), copied into this directory unchanged but for paths; the classification of the 17 unstable tests follows rung O's (explorations/compile-ladder/rung-walk-overflow/REPORT.md:40). The ladder subset driver is rung D's run-subset.sh with a source-directory variable (explorations/compile-ladder/rung-flat-tower/run-subset.sh).
- A precedent that repaired a defect is evidence of the same defect elsewhere: row 146's shape (a ZZ64 declared, a ZZ32 held) is the shape of row 428 (Ratio's num: ZZ holding a Long); both close by the same means, the typed binding or parameter converting by coercion once ZZ64 and ZZ are not supertypes of ZZ32 (section 5.5). I did not count the library's other sites of the shape by reading; the flat tower converts every such binding by coercion where walk checks a declared type, and the sites that needed an explicit conversion instead are the ones the comparison, the microGPT checks and the capability probe found (section 5.6).

Names added, grepped for competing declarations in ProjectFortress/tests/, every ProjectFortress/*_tests/ directory, ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/ and Library/: additiveIdentity, multiplicativeIdentity, exactValue, FlatTowerRungF. None found outside the library's own declaration.

## 3. The specification's derivation

- The tower. Instantiation exclusion (Specification/basic/types-vals-vars.tex:218-237) forbids a type below two instantiations of one generic, so ZZ32 cannot be both an Integral[\ZZ32\] and, through ZZ64, an Integral[\ZZ64\]; route A (POSITIONS.md:92) makes the leaves siblings. The number chapters still describe the nested tower (Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex, basic-integers.tex); they are rung T's.
- The coercions. Declared by the wider type (Specification/basic/conversions-coercions.tex:176-187), not inherited (:224-227), not chained (:127-132), so each pair of the table is declared on its own; a coercion applies only where the parameter's declared type is exactly the coerced-to type (:78-83), which settles two of the Q1 lines (section 9: longPrim's DIVIDES, whose self is an Integral[\ZZ64\], not a ZZ64). The table is the record's and nothing else: ZZ64 from ZZ32 and NN32; NN64 from NN32; ZZ from ZZ32, ZZ64, NN32 and NN64; QQ from the five integer types; RR64 from ZZ32. NN32 into RR64 stays explicit, and no site needed it.
- The algebra. ZZ is "a commutative ring and is totally ordered" (Specification/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:79), so Integral[\I\] extends MultiplicativeRing[\I\] as well as StandardTotalOrder[\I\]; that is what admits the integer types to PROD's bound (decision D2).
- Exact rationals. "Rational computations do not overflow" (Specification/basic/operators/opr-overview.tex:156, :197); numerator and denominator are declared ZZ (Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, QQ), so their products are unbounded.
- Equality across number types. "The comparison operators <, <=, =, >= and > allow any rational value to be compared numerically to any other rational value" (Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex:372-373); the integers are rationals in that chapter. This is the ground for decision D1.
- The reductions. A reduction expression takes optional static arguments (Specification/basic/expressions/reductions.tex:15-26), and the specification's desugaring of a clause-form sum is SUM[\N\] over SumReduction[\N\] (Specification/advanced/parallelism-locality/defining-generators.tex:147-157). Nothing in Specification/basic/ says how N is found when no argument fixes it; answer 7 has a clause form write it, and rung T writes the note (reductions.tex:23-25).
- Silent: whether a list literal of numerals has an element type an F-bounded big operator accepts. A numeral has type NaturalNumeral[\n,10,v\] and Literal[\v\], with the relation to the integer types left open in a note (Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:83-86), and a list expression's element type is the union of its elements' types (Specification/basic/expressions/aggregate.tex:105); so the specification does not say whether SUM <|1, 2, 3|> finds T = ZZ32. That is why section 12.1's refusal has home 3.

## 4. The test, first: the recorded failure and the recorded pass

ProjectFortress/tests/FlatTowerRungF.fss, in the form of roundBug.fss: a component exporting Executable whose run() asserts, one helper shown(v) giving a value and its run-time class (as IntSemanticsRungI.fss:14-18 does), each assertion's message citing its source, one comment line pointing at this report. Five groups, each run through group(g), which catches FailCalled so that every group reports; run() asserts that no group failed.
1. shape (:16-34): a ZZ32 is not a ZZ64, ZZ, QQ or RR64; a ZZ64 not a ZZ; an NN32 not an NN64; a ZZ not a QQ; a QQ not an RR64; every leaf a Number; a ZZ64 an AnyIntegral.
2. coercions (:36-77): x: ZZ64 = 2147483647 then x + 1 is 2147483648 : Long (row 146); every edge of the table by a typed binding, each with its run-time class (Long, UnsignedLong, BigNum, Ratio, Float); a ZZ32 plus a ZZ64 is a Long; a ZZ32 times an RR64 a Float; and four cross-type equalities against numbers.tex:372-373 (decision D1).
3. identities (:79-120): the verdict's three outcomes and the judgement's check 1: matOffset(0) with SUM[\ZZ32\] over an empty range in a function declared ZZ32 is 0 : Int; bare and clause-form RR64 sums, empty and not, declared RR64, are 0.0 : FloatLiteral and 3.75 : Float; a generic dotShaped[\T\] with SUM[\T\], empty and not, at RR64 and ZZ32, and the library's own Vector.dot through DOT, answer in the element type; empty and nonempty products typed ZZ32 and RR64 are 1 : Int, 24 : Int, 1.0 : FloatLiteral, 3.375 : Float; the ZZ64, ZZ and QQ zeros are 0 : Long, 0 : BigNum, 0 : Ratio; a ZZ64 sum of ZZ32 elements is 6 : Long; and strToFloat("3.25") is 3.25 : Float (section 5.8).
4. rational (:122-129): (widen(1) LSHIFT 62) < 1/4 and (widen(1) LSHIFT 61)/3 < 5/7 are false (row 428); +, DOT and / on parts beyond 32 bits give the exact Ratio.
5. products (:131-182): an object FlatView extending Matrix[\RR64,2,3\] over a Vector[\RR64,6\], in the shape of C4's parameter view, times its transpose, against the same product on an ordinary matrix, with exactly representable values; an integer matrix's product and BIG MAX over an integer array as controls; BIG MAX z over an RR64 array, the shape of the approved BIG MAX z; and the norms of a ZZ64 and a QQ vector (section 5.8).

## 5. The edit

### 5.1 The tower and the coercions

| Type | Extends | Excludes | Coercions declared |
|---|---|---|---|
| Number | AnyAdditiveGroup, AnyMultiplicativeRing; comprises RR64, QQ, AnyIntegral | | |
| RR64 | Number, StandardPartialOrder[\RR64\], StandardMinMax[\RR64\], AdditiveGroup[\RR64\], MultiplicativeRing[\RR64\]; comprises Float, FloatLiteral, RR32 | QQ, AnyIntegral | from ZZ32: asFloat(x) |
| QQ | Number, StandardPartialOrder[\QQ\], StandardMinMax[\QQ\], AdditiveGroup[\QQ\], MultiplicativeRing[\QQ\]; comprises Ratio | RR64, AnyIntegral | from ZZ32, ZZ64, NN32, NN64, ZZ: Ratio(x, 1) |
| AnyIntegral | Number; comprises ZZ, ZZ64, ZZ32, NN64, NN32 | | |
| Integral[\I\] | StandardTotalOrder[\I\], MultiplicativeRing[\I\], AnyIntegral | | |
| ZZ32 | AnyIntegral, Integral[\ZZ32\] | ZZ64, ZZ, NN64, NN32 | |
| ZZ64 | AnyIntegral, Integral[\ZZ64\] | ZZ, NN64, NN32 | from ZZ32: widen(x); from NN32: signed(widen(x)) |
| NN64 | AnyIntegral, Integral[\NN64\] | ZZ, NN32 | from NN32: widen(x) |
| ZZ | AnyIntegral, Integral[\ZZ\] | NN64, NN32 | from ZZ32, ZZ64: big(x); from NN32: big(signed(widen(x))); from NN64: big(signed(x)), plus 2^64 when negative |
| NN32 (FortressBuiltin) | AnyIntegral, Integral[\NN32\] | | |

Declarations: Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:276-606 and Library/FortressLibrary.fss:352-994; ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fsi and .fss for NN32 and RR32. RR32 stays below RR64 as a value object and gets no coercion. Every edge is exact; no other edge exists; the new test asserts each (group 2).

### 5.2 Number's catch-alls removed, and the methods restated

Number's 52 api declarations (57 in the component) are gone. Number keeps asFloat(self): RR64, now published in the api since String.fss and the tests call it, and a numeric opr = (decision D1). What the leaves had inherited from Number is restated where each leaf needs it:
- RR64 takes Number's operators and functions retyped to RR64, each as asFloat(self) op asFloat(b) (git show e5414f5bf:Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:276-336 against Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:286-378): =, =/=, <, <=, >, >=, CMP, MIN, MAX, MINMAX, unary and binary -, +, DOT, TIMES, juxtaposition, /, SQRT, the eighteen rounding-mode operators, |self|, ^, sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan, atan2, log, exp, floor, the floor and ceiling brackets, ceiling and truncate; and Number's zero 0.0 and one 1.0. What RR64 already declared (isNaN and its siblings, check, check_star, rawBits, MINNUM, MAXNUM, narrow) is unchanged. ^(self, b:Number) and atan2(self, x:Number) keep a Number parameter, because Float's own atan2(self, x:Number) is the native they reach and a retyped RR64 overload recursed against it (seen as a stack overflow in realArith during the first pass).
- QQ keeps its own operators unchanged; its zero and one are Ratio(0, 1) and Ratio(1, 1); isNumber is added.
- Integral[\I\] gains numerator(self): ZZ and denominator(self): ZZ (so an integer is a rational's parts), an abstract opr /(self, other:I): QQ, floor, ceiling and truncate as the identity, MINNUM and MAXNUM, and odd and even, moved from ZZ, where Number's catch-alls had served every integer type.
- Each leaf gets a / body answering a Ratio: ZZ32 and ZZ64 through big, NN32 and NN64 through typed bindings to ZZ, ZZ as before but always Ratio(a, b) (decision D3). ZZ32 gains narrow(self) = self and big(self); ZZ64 widen(self) = self.

### 5.3 SUM and PROD (answer 7)

additiveIdentity[\T extends AdditiveGroup[\T\]\]() and multiplicativeIdentity[\T extends MultiplicativeRing[\T\]\]() (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3107-3131) are typecases over __thrower[\T\], the () -> T witness of array1, with eight branches, narrowest first: () -> ZZ32, ZZ64, NN32, NN64, ZZ, QQ, RR32, RR64, each value through cast[\T\] (0, widen(0), unsigned(0), widen(unsigned(0)), big(0), Ratio(0, 1), narrow(0.0), 0.0, and the same with 1), and else => 0 or else => 1 as in the judgement's copy (decision D8). SumReduction[\T extends AdditiveGroup[\T\]\] joins a + b, ProdReduction[\T extends MultiplicativeRing[\T\]\] joins a b; SUM[\T\]() and PROD[\T\]() are BigReduction[\T,T\] of them, and the bare forms SUM[\T\](g) and PROD[\T\](g) keep their spelling (:3150-3178). The fusion pairs are restated generic: SumProdReductionPair[\T extends MultiplicativeRing[\T\]\], MaxSumReductionPair and MinSumReductionPair with both bounds, and SumReduction's two distribute overloads over MaxReduction[\T\] and MinReduction[\T\] (decision D9). The team's comment "Hack to permit any Number to work non-parametrically" goes with the block it described.

The run-time class of each identity is asserted in group 3 (0 : Int, 0 : Long, 0 : BigNum, 0 : Ratio, 0.0 : FloatLiteral, 1 : Int, 1.0 : FloatLiteral). The branch order puts every leaf before any supertype, so the text is right on a nested tower too; on the flat tower no leaf is below another except RR32 below RR64, listed first.

### 5.4 The three Number-typed big operators dropped

BIG MAXN, BIG MINN and BIG MINMAXN, their objects MaxReductionN, MinReductionN and MinMaxReductionN, the fusion pairs MaxNSumReductionPair and MinNSumReductionPair, the distribute overloads that named them, and the DistributesOver[...] clauses of SumReduction and ProdReduction that named them are removed, in the api (git show e5414f5bf:Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1841-1887) as in the component (git show e5414f5bf:Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3043-3150). The reason, as the decision gives it: their identity is the rational -1/0 or 1/0, a value no integer or float fold can hold, and a maximum's identity is not carried by a coercion (explorations/reviews/max-min-identities-judgement.md sections 1 and 4). Completeness: grep for MAXN, BIG MINN, MINMAXN, ReductionN and NSumReductionPair over Library/, ProjectFortress/ (tests, library_tests, LibraryBuiltin) and the demos under explorations/ finds none; the only file that still names them is the judgement's own probe explorations/reviews/max-min-identities-judgement/MaxMinWalk.fss, a record of what they did, which no longer runs. The marker trait DistributesOver stays declared (nothing names it now but a commented-out block of Library/Generator2.fss:58-70).

### 5.5 The rational arithmetic made exact (row 428), and row 146

Ratio(num: ZZ, den: ZZ) and QQ's operators keep their text (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:544-639). On the nested tower a ZZ64 or ZZ32 was a ZZ, so a Ratio's parts could be Longs and Ints and its cross-products wrapped. On the flat tower ZZ is a sibling, so every value reaching a ZZ field or parameter is converted to a BigNum by ZZ's coercions (walk converts at a constructor's parameter), and numerator(self) and denominator(self) answer BigNums: the products in <, +, DOT and / cannot overflow. Group 4 asserts the two comparisons of row 428 false and the exact +, DOT and / beyond 32 bits. The same mechanism closes row 146: x: ZZ64 = 2147483647 now holds a Long, by ZZ64's coercion from ZZ32 at the typed binding, and x + 1 is 2147483648 (group 2).

### 5.6 Library sites written differently, with the reason

Static arguments written, the eleven of the judgement's section 4 A: SUM[\T\] in Vector.dot (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2303), Matrix.rmul and Matrix.lmul (:2653, :2658) and Library/Sparse.fss:96; SUM[\ZZ32\] in strToInt (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4255) and strToFloat (:4271), Library/ChunkedSparseArray.fss:161 and :163, Library/PrefixMap.fss:380, Library/PrefixSet.fss:374 and Library/SkipList.fss:208.

Explicit conversions, each where a value relied on a link of the old chain that the table leaves explicit (ZZ64, ZZ, QQ or NN into RR64; ZZ into ZZ64), or on a coercion walk does not apply:
- Library/Timing.fss:30-32: asFloat(duration) / 10.0^9 (and ^6, 1000.0); duration is a ZZ64, and ZZ64 into RR64 is lossy, so explicit (POSITIONS.md:159).
- Library/Random.fss:199: asFloat(9007199254740992); the numeral 2^53 is a ZZ64.
- Library/Random.fss:270, :278-280 (MersenneTwister): one: N = 1 replaces 1 asif N, since asif does not convert (explorations/reviews/flattening-questions-ways.md:575-577) and the typed binding does, N being ZZ64 at every instantiation (Library/Random.fss:355-363).
- Library/String.fss:508: asFloat(ssize) / asFloat(numFlat) replaces ssize / (numFlat asif Number), which reached Number's catch-all /.
- Library/Format.fss:70: n = widen(|/(val / base)\|); val / base is a QQ now, its ceiling a ZZ, used as a ZZ64.
- Library/ChunkedSparseArray.fss:54: fill(widen(0), emptyArray); a numeral inside a tuple argument is not converted by walk (row 395).
- Library/QuickCheck.fss: genZZ.perturb's recursive argument big(widen(obj) LSHIFT 32), keeping the base's 64-bit shift (decision D10, provisional row 431); genQQ.perturb uses DIV for its integral quotients, since / answers a Ratio; genRR64.generate converts its ZZ64 with asFloat.
- Library/ReflectiveQuickCheck.fss:149-150: NN64 and NN32 get genZZ as their generator; without them the reflective generator for Number recursed without end once NN32 and NN64 were no longer ZZs.
- Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4271 (strToFloat) and :2383 (the vector norm), section 5.8.
- Inside the tower: NN64's and NN32's / bind their operands to ZZ by typed bindings; ZZ's coercion from NN64 adds 2^64 to a negative signed value; simplestRationalBetween binds its result q: QQ, since its infinite case r = 1/0 is a Ratio that Ratio(r, 1) would have wrapped.

### 5.7 FortressBuiltin

NN32 (ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fsi, .fss) extends AnyIntegral and Integral[\NN32\] instead of StandardTotalOrder[\NN32\] and NN64, and gains its / answering a Ratio. RR32's 32 natives that took b:Number take b:RR64, and RR32's and Float's MIN and MAX answer RR64 and MINMAX (RR64,RR64), where they answered Number: with Number's catch-alls gone, walk's overload check refused RR32's PLUS_UP beside RR64's ("first parameter list is a subtype ... first result is not a subtype"), and the scalar-extension MAX beside StandardTotalOrder's generic one. An RR32 with an integer now meets it by ZZ32's coercion into RR64; with a QQ or a ZZ64 it needs asFloat.

### 5.8 Three edits made after the first pass, each test-first

After the three passes, the capability probe and a probe of the eleven SUM sites found two library bodies that still relied on the nested tower, and the body-level check found one type error in the rung's own new code. Each was asserted in the new test first and captured failing, then repaired; the passes that read the landed library were then run again (section 0).
- strToFloat (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4267-4272): 1.0 (SUM[\ZZ32\][...] ...)/(10^(|frac|)) parses as 1.0 juxtaposed with an integer quotient, now a Ratio, and RR64 has no juxtaposition with a QQ (QQ into RR64 is lossy, so explicit): every call was refused (probes/strtofloat-flat-before.txt: "args = (1.0,Ratio)"), where the base answered 3.25 : Float (probes/strtofloat-base.txt). Now asFloat((SUM[\ZZ32\][...] ...)/(10^(|frac|))), the same value (probes/strtofloat-flat-after.txt; the probe probes/StrToFloatProbe.fss). No test, demo or model calls strToFloat (C4 has its own parser, explorations/run-c4/src/FlatData.fss:5), which is why the passes did not see it.
- The vector norm (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2383): SQRT squaredNorm(me) on a ZZ64, NN32, NN64, ZZ or QQ vector was refused (the SQRT of a type with no coercion into RR64; probes/failure-norm.txt, "args = (25: ZZ64)"); on the base it ran through Number's SQRT. Now SQRT asFloat(squaredNorm(me)), the same value for every leaf (section 12, the capability probe).
- Number's = (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:358-377): its else branch called sameRational(a: QQ, b: QQ) with two Numbers; walk converted at the call, but the checker refused it ("(QQ, QQ)->Boolean is not applicable to an argument of type ((Number & {RR64, QQ, AnyIntegral}), Number)"), rightly, since a typecase's else does not narrow and no coercion is declared from Number. exactValue(x: Number): QQ now converts each exact leaf by a typed binding, each typecase clause binding its value (q: QQ => q, z: ZZ32 => do q: QQ = z; q end, ...), the form of the library's own cast (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:33-37): a first version that narrowed the unbound identifier drew 16 checker errors of its own ("Right-hand side has type Number, but declared type is QQ"), since the checker narrows only a bound clause. The answers are the same throughout (the four equalities of group 2 pass before and after both edits).

## 6. Decisions taken inside the rung, each with the alternative not taken

- D1. Number keeps one numeric opr = across number types (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:355-377; api :280-283): two exact numbers compare as rationals through exactValue, and a float compares with any number through asFloat. Alternative: Number without =, as route A's "Number without its catch-all operators" reads literally. Not taken because the library's own opr =(a:Any, b:Any) = a SEQV b would then answer every mixed comparison, so 3 = 3.0 and widen(3) = big(3) would be false with no error, and team tests that compare numbers of different run-time types (CovariantTest's List[\Number\] against List[\ZZ32\], assert(x, y) over mixed values) would change silently; and the specification says rationals compare numerically (Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex:372-373). This is a decision for Pavol's eye: it is one declaration more on Number than "without its catch-alls".
- D2. Integral[\I\] extends MultiplicativeRing[\I\] beside StandardTotalOrder[\I\] (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:644), so the integers meet PROD's bound and have a one. Alternative: the flat sketch's AdditiveGroup only, which would leave PROD[\ZZ32\] outside its bound. Ground: "ZZ is a commutative ring" (Specification/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:79). The integration review warned that MultiplicativeRing's ^ answers T while the integers' ^ answers RR64 (explorations/reviews/numeric-hierarchy-integration-review.md section 2); walk does not check that, and the checker's body-level errors (section 13) show no new one from it; it is noted, not solved.
- D3. Integer / always answers a Ratio, and a Ratio whose denominator is 1 prints as its numerator (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:628-629). On the base, ZZ's / answered a ZZ when the quotient was whole (git show e5414f5bf:Library/FortressLibrary.fss:891-897), which a QQ-typed / can no longer do, a ZZ not being a QQ. Alternative: print n/1. Not taken because every whole quotient the tests print would change ("3" to "3/1"); with this spelling none did.
- D4. Integral[\I\] keeps AnyIntegral among its supertypes. Alternative: drop it, which the checker's comprises rule would prefer ("AnyIntegral has a comprises clause but its immediate subtype Integral is not eligible to extend it", reported before and after). Not taken because without it walk's overload check refuses C4's generic array operators beside Integral's generic ones (the arrays exclude Number, and so AnyIntegral, only through that link), and the microGPT check failed; with it both checks pass 40 of 40.
- D5. Number keeps a comprises clause, { RR64, QQ, AnyIntegral }. Alternative: none, as route A does not ask for one. Not taken because walk's overload check needs the exclusions it gives to accept the scalar-extension MAX beside StandardTotalOrder's generic MAX ("excluding types"), as today's comprises { RR64 } gave them.
- D6. asFloat(self): RR64 is published in Number's api; it was a component-only method. Alternative: a new conversion function. Not taken: the library's bodies already use asFloat, and Library/String.fss and the respelled tests need it visible.
- D7. RR32's natives take RR64 where they took Number, and RR32's and Float's MIN, MAX and MINMAX answer RR64 (section 5.7). Alternative: keep Number parameters, which walk's overload check refuses beside RR64's own operators once Number declares none.
- D8. The identity witness has eight branches, the number leaves narrowest first with RR32 before RR64, and keeps the judgement's else => 0 and else => 1 (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3117, :3130). Alternative: else => cast[\T\](0), which the checker would type as T, or a throw. Not taken, to follow the judgement's measured copy (explorations/reviews/sum-replacement-judgement/variants/sumlib.py:27, :35); the checker reports one error on each ("Function body has type OR(T,IntLiteral), but declared return type is T", section 13). The branch values go through cast[\T\], as the verdict proposes.
- D9. The fusion pairs SumProdReductionPair, MaxSumReductionPair and MinSumReductionPair and SumReduction's two distribute overloads are restated generic, not dropped; the judgement allowed either ("restated in T or dropped for the rung", explorations/reviews/sum-replacement-judgement.md, section 4 A). Kept because Library/Generator2.fss:73 and :168 call r.distribute(q), and Generator2Test's maximum prefix sum takes the fused path with them. Cost, measured: the checker reports the restated types ill-formed, 6 reports at 4 sites (MaxReduction[\T\] and MinReduction[\T\] in SumReduction's distribute, MaxSumReductionPair[\T\] and MinSumReductionPair[\T\] in their bodies), because T extends AdditiveGroup[\T\] does not give StandardMax[\T\]. The specification's remedy is a where clause on the method (Specification/basic/trait-parameters.tex:285-310), which "are not supported yet" (Specification/basic/functions.tex:15-19); provisional row 433.
- D10. genZZ.perturb keeps the base's 64-bit shift, big(widen(obj) LSHIFT 32) (Library/QuickCheck.fss:322). Alternative: RSHIFT 32, which is what peeling 32 bits at a time evidently means. Not taken because it changes the generated values of every QuickCheck test that reaches it; provisional row 431 records the defect.

Not taken because it changes the generated values of every QuickCheck test that reaches it; provisional row 431 records the defect.

- D12. strToFloat converts the quotient with asFloat and keeps the approved SUM[\ZZ32\] (its elements are Ints: walk's ZZ32 ^ answers an Int, probes/strtofloat-flat-after.txt "10^k : Int"). Alternative: SUM[\RR64\] over converted terms, which departs from the approved list.
- D13. The team-test respellings (section 9): typed comprehensions (<|[\ZZ32\] ...|>) where a list's element type walk takes from run-time classes fails a new F-bound; asFloat where a value relied on ZZ64, ZZ, QQ or Number reaching RR64; widen where a ZZ32 met a generic Integral method or a generic function's ZZ64 parameter; List[\Number\] where a list mixes integers and floats. Alternative for each: the smallest other spelling that keeps the value, e.g. a float literal (fib13, vectorOps, asifTest took that form where it keeps the value).

## 7. The comparison: what changed when the tower flipped

Every file of ProjectFortress/tests/ but the new test, 407 files (explorations/compile-ladder/rung-flat-tower/count-list.txt), under walk, one JVM per test with private caches, four at a time, FORTRESS_THREADS=1 (rung O's count-run.sh, copied as explorations/compile-ladder/rung-flat-tower/count-run.sh), in three passes: base A (before any library edit), the edit, base B (the 40 edited library, test and model files checked out at e5414f5bf, then restored). Each pass is headed by its machine line (probes/passes/machine-baseA.txt, machine-edit.txt, machine-baseB.txt; start and end times in probes/passes/pass-timing.txt). The edit pass that the comparison reads is the third, on the landed library at c02b558c1 (probes/passes/machine-edit.txt). The first, at 077beba2d, and the second, at aa6ae506a, gave the same classification test for test (probes/passes/compare-normalised-edit1.txt, compare-normalised-edit2.txt); the third's outputs differ from the second's only in the 17 unstable files, and the second's from the first's only in those and in the three whose messages print library line numbers, moved by the section 5.8 edits.

Normalised, and nothing else (rung D's compare-normalised.py, Q2 = (a) of batch 5): Java line numbers of printed stack frames, identity hashes, and Fortress source positions in a file the edit changed, mapped back through the edit's line map.

Result (probes/passes/compare-normalised.txt): 407 tests, 383 same, 4 normalised, 3 changed, 17 unstable, 0 missing. Exit codes are 336 rc=0, 64 rc=1 and 7 rc=255 in all five passes (probes/passes/rc-distribution.txt): no exit code changed.
- Normalised: XXXFnRenderRungS and XXXTupleSevenRungS (library positions in their expected error), taskTrace2 and taskTrace3 (identity hashes).
- Changed, each with its cause (captures in probes/changed/, base A, base B and edit):
  - Region: "Just(17) at Global" becomes "Just(17.0) at Global". ProjectFortress/tests/Region.fss:20 stores Just[\RR64\](17); the constructor's parameter is declared RR64, and walk now converts the ZZ32 by RR64's coercion from ZZ32 (on the nested tower the Int already was an RR64 and was kept). Cause: a coercion now applied, of the table.
  - simpleBig: p7's printed list shows every element as a float (2.0, 3.0, 4.0, ...) where it showed 2, 3.0, 4, .... The line is respelled under Q1 (section 9): p7 : List[\RR64\] = <|[\RR64\] asFloat(body(x + y)) | ...|>, because body(x:ZZ32): RR64 returns its Int unconverted under walk (row 387) and an Int is no longer an RR64. The assertion SUM p7 = 605.0 is unchanged and passes. Cause: a respelled line.
  - XXXArrayLiteralArgRungC: its expected failure is unchanged, rc 1 in all passes, "Failed to find any matching overload, args = (3: ZZ32,(1,2): (Int,Int))" at its line 8 (row 49); the overload list the message prints names RR64's and the leaves' operators where it named Number's and RR32's b:Number natives. Cause: restated methods (sections 5.2 and 5.7).
- Unstable: ArrayListQuick, CovCollTest, HeapTest, PureListQuick, QuickCheckTest, ShuffleTest, SkipListTest, TimingTests, TreapTest, WordCountSmall, abortBlock, buffons, nestedTransactions1 to 4 and quicksortTest: base A and base B differ, all exit 0 in every pass. The same seventeen rung O found, with the same kinds of difference: timings, random data, thread interleaving (explorations/compile-ladder/rung-walk-overflow/REPORT.md:40). probes/passes/unstable-check.txt lists, per file, the lines where A and B differ and where the edit differs from A: for 15 the edit differs only where A and B do; for TreapTest and abortBlock the edit differs elsewhere too, and by hand these are random picks (TreapTest: "Azero", "Azero" and "Athree" at line 3 in A, B and the edit) and the count of aborted transactions (abortBlock: 2,883, 2,966 and 1,796 "Aborting" lines); in the second edit pass QuickCheckTest was a third such, its random data changing its length (53, 55 and 56 lines). Not a stop (POSITIONS.md:167).
- XXXInheritedOverload, which the record lists as unstable citing row 430, printed the same in all three passes here; row 430 says its message order varies with the JVM's flags and the library's contents, so an equal output is not evidence that it is stable.

The tests the record names as must-stay-green all print the same in the three passes: IntSemanticsRungI, WrapOperatorsRungD, ArrayScalarExtension, ArrayOperatorsBesideLibrary, rung C's expected failures (XXXCoercionStaticRungC, XXXCoercionStaticNarrowRungC, XXXCoercionReturnRungC, XXXCoercionGenericFnRungC, XXXCoercionGenericTraitRungC, XXXCoercionTupleOverloadRungC) and XXXFixedWidthOverflowRungB. XXXArrayLiteralArgRungC keeps its verdict (above).

## 8. The thread-count differential

The manifest sets writesState: a reduction's identity is joined at each split of a parallel generator, so every differential of a reduction runs at FORTRESS_THREADS=1 and =4.
- At one thread: the three-pass comparison of section 7 covers every test, the new test runs at one thread (probes/pass-postedit-threads1.txt), and the two microGPT checks run at one thread (section 10).
- At four threads: the new test passes on the landed library (probes/pass-postedit-threads4.txt).
